reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows stepwise reduction, not simultaneous, and attributes single-phase formation to increased dilution in five-element systems rather than to rapid heating freezing a randomized state. The key premises about simultaneous reduction and diffusion-limited freezing are not supported and are partly contradicted by the cited text.
premises: Rapid heating forces simultaneous reduction of all metal precursors
Simultaneous reduction limits atomic diffusion during nucleation
Limited diffusion freezes a randomized single-phase alloy before segregation
Slower heating permits sufficient diffusion, causing phase separation or inhomogeneity
